days.title: We spent two months solving a problem that did not exist
days.angle: retraction — publish our own correction before anyone asks for it
days.proof_plan: The July 2026 conclusion ('this render model is deprecated and non-commercially licensed, we must swap') was WRONG and is retracted in-wiki on 2026-09-20. The deprecation covered the vendor's own endpoints, not the API we actually call, which never deprecated it and billed us on 2026-09-19. The non-commercial licence binds self-hosting, not API callers. DO NOT restate the original deprecation claim as if it were true.
days.method_layer: The model was dropped anyway — on image quality, a reason that will not expire. The register entry was corrected the same day with the note that a model rejected on QUALITY is not 'best-but-not-implementable', it is simply not best.
days.notes: Opens W40 on integrity. Publishing your own retraction is rare and costs nothing here because the decision did not change — only the reason did.

days.title: Phantom walls had three different causes. We fixed one.
days.angle: a real win, published with the limit on it
days.proof_plan: 31 wall segments, each verified against the plan image. Zero phantom walls in the open spine. Spatial evals 0 fails, 99 tests green. Designer verbatim: 'the most beautiful geometry logs ... in every way perfect, almost perfect.'
days.method_layer: MANDATORY CAVEAT, do not publish the quote without it: the segments are BANDS, not a graph, and are DERIVED from the already-corrected model plus QA — NOT acquired from a semantic mask. Phantom walls had three sources and this fixed the rendering one only. The acquisition bet is SUSPECT and still UNTESTED (reviewed 2026-07-06).
days.notes: The week's clear win. Deliberately placed early so W40 is not five days of self-criticism.

days.title: 'It's not editable' turned out to be three different bugs
days.angle: build receipt — a real fix, measured against hand-computed truth
days.proof_plan: A designer reported fixtures could not be moved on the plan canvas. It resolved into two unrelated causes, neither obvious: a canvas layer built with listening disabled, so the hit graph was dead; and a calibration anchored to the four corners of the image, assuming the plan bleeds edge to edge. px/ft X 47.82 -> 40.31 against a hand-computed truth of 40.30. px/ft Y 41.96 -> 40.39 (truth 40.39). Anisotropy 1.1396 -> 0.998 (truth 1.000). Fixtures had been drawn 18.6% too wide and up to ~1.7 ft out of place; one chair box sat outside the building. Test suite 859 -> 871 green.
days.method_layer: Durable lesson for both audiences: auto-derived config must announce itself. The calibration was wrong for months because a plausible number displayed with no provenance. Include that the falsifier fired in the same session — aspect-only outline detection picked an interior rectangle on another plan. A fallback indistinguishable from a real answer is a bug, not a fallback.
days.notes: SWAPPED 2026-09-20, replacing idea-020. idea-020's central fact (the model supplying the wrong country's state emblem) cannot be published under the naming clearance on record — it would reveal the chamber's emblem/portrait arrangement. idea-019 carries comparable engineering weight, has hard before/after numbers against hand-computed truth, and has ZERO client exposure: it is about our own canvas tool, not the client's room. days.title: Our own quality score ranked the worst render first and the shipped one last
days.angle: contrarian — earned, and aimed at ourselves before anyone else
days.proof_plan: Same control image, same room. The pass-through render — the model handing the control back untouched, the worst output of the set — scored the HIGHEST covered_ratio at 0.7885. The render Nine Bricks actually accepted scored the LOWEST at 0.5216. Reference point on the same control: nano-banana-pro round-3 base 0.7527. Whole pilot was 4 renders, ~$0.11 — cost-to-run only, never framed as client savings.
days.method_layer: The conclusion: covered_ratio is a floor to clear, never a ranking. Highest-scoring idea in the backlog (40.50) and it was on no plan before the 2026-09-20 wiki audit.
